messages:
Alex: FYI ran a high-concurrency sweep overnight. At concurrency ~700 p99 shot from ~240ms -> ~1.4s, p95 mostly stable.
Maria: Any obvious correlates? model / seq / microbatch config?
Alex: redwood-v1-13b, seq=512 typical, microbatch target=6, workers=64, kv_entries ~= 120k. Short log snip:
```
[2026-03-09T03:12:08Z] req 0x1a2: route->dev2 microbatch=3
[2026-03-09T03:12:08Z] kvcache: miss prefix=user:ctx:... new_entry; entries=120128
[2026-03-09T03:12:08Z] kvcache: evict 10 entries (LRU scan)
[2026-03-09T03:12:09Z] kernel: chosen=matmul_opt; fallback->generic_gemm (OOM soft-fail)
[2026-03-09T03:12:09Z] latency p99=1.42s
```
Devon: Sampling/trace summary: CPU spin and GPU memcpy stalls spike during eviction windows. KV miss rate increases ~2.5x for ~15-25s bursts. Microbatch distribution collapses to many tiny batches [1,2,2,3,6] during spikes.
Jordan: Classic amplification: KV thrash -> many tiny microbatches -> repeated kernel select/setup -> tail amplification. Two knobs to try: softer eviction (raise capacity or change policy) and microbatch floor to avoid churn.
Alex: I tried raising mb target->12 on a small pool: baseline throughput +9% but p99 worsened to ~1.7s. Looks like larger batches increased queueing for missed-key requests which then block a batch.
Lee: Also watch KV eviction scan lock contention. LRU full scans under hot-key skew cause pauses. LFU-approx or segmenting the cache by prefix shard might help.
Maria: Kernel switching is expensive if selection is done per-batch and depends on microbatch size. We should add a pin for kernel variant per-model or per-replica to reduce churn. Quantized kernel pin helped in previous runs.
Alex: Quick A/B prototype: pinned kernel=quant_gemm on one replica set. When kv hit rate >90% p99 ~480ms. But as hit rate dropped to ~55% under higher concurrency p99 climbed back to ~950ms.
Devon: Alternative: per-request fast-path for misses: if a request sees a miss, mark it as "fast-lane" and execute unbatched low-latency path (more kernel launches but avoids blocking other requests). That isolates miss cost from batch tail.
Jordan: Tradeoffs: fast-lane increases GPU kernel launch counts and overhead but prevents a single miss from inflating one batch's latency. Might be good as an adaptive option when miss-rate > threshold.
Alex: Proposed test matrix tonight (3x 30m runs):
- Config A: increase kv max_entries +15%, eviction policy soft-LRU, microbatch bounds floor=4 ceil=12, kernel pinned to quant_gemm.
- Config B: same as A + enable per-request fast-lane for detected misses.
- Control: current prod config.
Lee: I'll stage the eviction change and run a synthetic with skewed-hot-prefix arrival to stress it.
Maria: I'll add metrics to capture: per-request path (batched vs fast-lane), kernel-switch count, kv hit/miss hist, microbatch size histogram, and per-batch queue wait time. If we see kernel-switch > X/sec that's a red flag.
Devon: Also capture lock-wait samples during eviction windows (perf/trace) to confirm contention vs algorithmic eviction cost.
SRE-bot: incident:sev3 created for p99-regression on prod-serving (https://redwood-infra/incident/IS-2026-0527)
Alex: Thanks. I'll run the tests and post TL;DR + raw traces here. If either A or B reduces p99 by >40% without >5% throughput regression we can promote.
Jordan: If A reduces miss-induced tails but B further isolates variance, my vote is B. Need to watch token-cost impact.
Alex: Agreed. Rolling changes to staging now. Will ping when results are in. :thumbsup:
